newsitem.title: USA: Cagle's fined, OSHA raises safety concern.
newsitem.headline: Cagle's fined, OSHA raises safety concern.

text.p: The U.S. Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA) on Tuesday said it was fining Atlanta-based poultry producer Cagle's Inc $1.27 million for alleged safety violations.
Cagle's has 15 days to contest OSHA's charges of numerous alleged "willful and serious safety violations" at its Macon, Ga., facility.

OSHA said it moved to slap a fine against the poultry producer after an employee lost part of a finger while cleaning moving equipment on September 10. The previous year, another Cagle's worker lost a foot and a third lost a finger.

OSHA said inspectors found that Cagle's failed to use required procedures to ensure that hazardous machinery was turned off during repairs and maintenance work. OSHA said the company failed to respond to employee safety concerns.
In April 1996, Cagle's Macon plant was cited by OSHA and the company ultimately paid a fine of $88,000, OSHA said.
